result.title: Grounding Image Composition with Label-Conditioned Visual Evidence
result.summary: Image composition labels such as center, diagonal, or rule of thirds describe visual structure rather than object categories. KU-PCP provides image-level labels and class-specific geometric elements, but does not show which visible regions people associate with each of its nine classes. We introduce KU-PCP Elements (KU-PCPE), a label-conditioned region-evidence benchmark for photographic composition. Given an image and a label already judged applicable, the task is to segment the visible regions that explain why the label applies. KU-PCPE contains 4,093 single-annotator training masks and a 1,327-task expert test split with three masks per image-label task. The annotations also include exploratory segment-versus-line ratings that describe whether region or semantic-guideline evidence better explains the label. A held-out expert reaches .867 Dice against the other experts, while the strongest deployable model reaches .664, a proposal oracle .672, and the best vision-language model (VLM) proposal selector .395. KU-PCPE exposes the gap between recognizing a composition label and grounding the human-aligned visual evidence that makes it plausible in a particular image.

AI.brief_summary: 构建 KU-PCPE 基准：给定图像与已判定适用的构图标签，要求分割出支持该标签的可见区域，含 4,093 个单标注训练掩码与 1,327 个专家测试任务，并评估 VLM 作为候选区域选择器的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「识别标签易、定位支持标签的视觉证据难」的落差及区域与语义引导线孰更有效的标注，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与答案是否真正依赖具体证据的评测设计。
